Direct_Dehydrative_Boron_Catalysis.title: Direct Dehydrative Amidation – Boron Catalysis
Direct_Dehydrative_Boron_Catalysis.description: Aryl borane/borate catalysts promote condensation of carboxylic acids with amines with water removal.

entries.substrate_class: Aliphatic/aromatic carboxylic acids with primary/secondary amines
boron_partners: molecular sieves or azeotrope for H2O removal

catalytic_systems.system_name: Aryl borane (highly electron-poor) at mild T

entries.operational_notes: Maintain efficient water removal (molecular sieves or Dean–Stark). Avoid strong bases that poison Lewis acidic borane.
entries.scope_limitations: Strongly basic amines and coordinating substrates can bind borane; higher loading or additives may be required.

Triarylsilanol_Catalysis.title: Direct Amidation – Triarylsilanol Catalysts
Triarylsilanol_Catalysis.description: Triaryl silanols (Ar3SiOH) catalyse dehydrative amide formation under azeotropic water removal.

entries.substrate_class: Broad scope acids with primary/secondary amines
entries.operational_notes: Employ azeotropic water removal; catalyst loadings of 2–10 mol% are typical depending on sterics.
entries.scope_limitations: Poorly nucleophilic amides (e.g., anilides) may require higher temperature or prolonged times.

supporting_evidence.quote: Paraphrase; OCR pending: Triarylsilanols (Ar3SiOH) can catalyse the direct amidation of carboxylic acids with amines under azeotropic water removal.
Paraphrase; OCR pending: Representative protocols employ 2–10 mol% catalyst, toluene or CPME, and Dean–Stark or sieves to remove water.

Biocatalytic_Amidation.title: Biocatalytic Amide Bond Formation

entries.operational_notes: Maintain suitable pH and cofactors. Enzyme stability benefits from co-solvents at low percentage for hydrophobic substrates.
entries.scope_limitations: Enzyme specificity; scale-up may require immobilization and continuous removal of water/ammonia.

Reagent_Based_Coupling.title: Reagent-Based Couplings (Carbodiimide, Uronium, etc.)
